title: Comparative assessment of large language models for microbial phenotype assignment.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the Zenodo v2.0.0 archive (21.6 MB zip, MIT licence; the record redirects to 19693395). Opened ground_truth_WA.csv (3,876 species x 13 traits, 0 duplicate names) and ground_truth_LA.csv (15,257 species, 1 duplicate). Counted non-missing labels per trait: e.g. WA gram 3,870, spore 3,642, motility 2,977, biofilm only 255, health association only 12. Opened s6_complete.csv (69,794 LLM calls: 18 models x 3,884 species, query date column) and knowledge_accuracy_wa/la.csv (421,752 and 305,150 long-format rows: model, self-rated knowledge level, species, trait, ground truth, prediction). Also wa_with_gcount.txt (Google hit counts) and the R script that built the labels from bugphyzz.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Balanced-accuracy numbers (best ~0.77 Gemini 2.5 Pro; spore 89.8%, biofilm 53.0% means), the 57-model hallucination test, the 81% literature support for new calls, and the deep-learning comparison model (not identified in the text I retrieved). Whether bugphyzz labels include ancestral-state-reconstruction (inferred-by-phylogeny) entries was not checked: the R script calls importBugphyzz() with no Evidence filter.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo zip downloaded without login (verified); MIT licence.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Curated trait labels are columns in ground_truth_WA/LA.csv, and LLM predictions sit next to them in knowledge_accuracy_*.csv (verified). Correct/incorrect per LLM call is a direct comparison, not a construction.

a3_inputs_present.note: For the in-hand task (meta-model over LLM calls) inputs are present: 18-31 LLM predictions, self-rated knowledge level, Google hit count. Genomes are NOT included; a genome-based model would need name-to-assembly lookups for thousands of species.

a4_units_stated.note: Categorical labels with a fixed vocabulary (e.g. 'gram stain negative', 'biosafety level 2'); no physical units involved (verified).

a5_enough_rows.note: 3,876 WA species, with ~2,000-3,870 labels per main trait; 15,257 LA species (verified). Biofilm (255) and health association (12) are too sparse to use.

a6_fits_laptop.note: All tables together are under 200 MB; pandas on CPU is enough.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Paper says WA 3,884 and LA 15,256; files hold 3,876 WA rows (3,884 in the prediction table, as in the paper's Fig. 4 '3876 species') and 15,257 LA rows. Small, explainable gaps.

a8_label_provenance.note: Labels come from bugphyzz, a harmonized curation of BacDive and other sources. Risk: bugphyzz also contains annotations inferred by phylogeny (ancestral state reconstruction), and the label-building R script applies no evidence filter, so some labels may be predictions. Not fatal for judging LLMs, but unverified.

B1.why: Ground-truth table plus long-format prediction table, joined on binomial species name; works but a name join (verified).

B2.why: CSVs parse, but mixed dtypes and 'TRUE'/'True'/'FALSE' string variants need normalizing (seen in files).

B3.why: Labels harmonized by bugphyzz, but sources mix BacDive, literature and possibly phylogenetic inference.

B4.why: No censored values; missing labels are plain NaN (verified).

B5.why: One duplicate in LA; repo has multiple near-duplicate versions of s6 tables (s6_old, which_file_test) to pick between.

B6.why: Column names self-explanatory; no data dictionary; which file was used for which figure is not documented.

C1.why: A 'when to trust an LLM' model is informative either way, but mostly confirms the paper's own confidence finding.

C2.why: Genome-based trait predictors exist and are open (BacDive random forests, MiGenPro); LLM meta-models largely unexplored beyond paper's ensemble.

C3.why: Weak unique-application angle: combine LLM calls with genome predictors for obscure species.

C4.why: Phenotype annotation is manual expert curation from literature and lab tests.

C5.why: Published per-trait balanced accuracy per LLM, best single model ~0.77 mean (paper).

D1.why: No natural backbone for species-name inputs; protein models only if genomes are fetched separately.

D2.why: Embedding whole proteomes of thousands of species with ESM-2 on CPU is days of compute.

D3.why: Data MIT licence; bugphyzz is open (Artistic-2.0 Bioconductor package).

E1.why: Genus- or order-held-out splits possible from species names; phylogeny tree in repo.

E2.why: Hundreds of genera; paper lists 30 orders with ≥10 species.

E3.why: Majority class, best single LLM, majority vote across LLMs.

E4.why: 18-31 LLMs per species give disagreement; label noise itself not estimable without replicates.

E5.why: Known effect: accuracy rises with self-rated knowledge and Google hit count (paper).

E6.why: Label shuffling and dropping LLM-confidence features are straightforward.

E7.why: LA set (15,257 species) as second panel; BacDive genome-based predictions as an independent source.

E8.why: Per-model balanced accuracies can be recomputed from knowledge_accuracy_wa.csv.

G1.why: Only binomial names in output files; NCBI taxonomy IDs exist in bugphyzz but were dropped.

G2.why: BacDive and GTDB/NCBI assemblies joinable on NCBI taxonomy ID after re-export from bugphyzz.

G3.why: One species maps to many genomes/strains; need a type-strain collapse rule.

G4.why: Where do LLMs beat genome models and vice versa, by species obscurity? Marginal new science.

H1.why: Both True and False recorded for most binary traits (verified counts).

H2.why: Thousands of species across phyla, but all from one harmonized resource and biased to cultured type strains.

H3.why: Claim can be stated precisely (see honest_claim_h3).

H4.why: Paper discusses sparse traits and naming limits; possible phylogeny-inferred labels not mentioned.

I1.why: Microbial database curators (BacDive, bugphyzz/Waldron lab) and microbiome analysts; no specific decision.

I2.why: Could set a filter for accepting LLM-filled annotations; marginal.

I3.why: Decision is accept/reject an annotation; precision at a confidence cut-off is the metric.

I4.why: Majority vote plus knowledge filter may already capture most of the gain.

J1.why: Mostly tabular stacking and calibration; little representation learning.

J2.why: Traits like Gram stain are easy to sanity-check; pathogenicity labels less so.

J3.why: A per-trait accept/reject curve is shareable at every stage.

J4.why: No budget set; roughly one to two weeks.

existing_models.name: BacDive genome-based random forest trait models (Communications Biology 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: Cross-validated on 15,938 BacDive strains with genomes for 8 traits (Gram, spores, motility, oxygen, temperature); exact split not checked.

existing_models.name: NLP plus genome bacterial phenotype prediction (NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics 2025, lqaf174)
Unsupervised whole-genome representation learning of bacterial phenotypes (bioRxiv 2025)
The paper's own LLM benchmark and ensemble (zero-shot LLMs, best ~0.77 mean balanced accuracy)
existing_models.score_and_split: All WA species, no train/test split (zero-shot).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Names without stable binomials, recently reclassified taxa and newly described species; hallucination by taxon left to future work.

backbone.name: None natural for name-only inputs; ESM-2 (protein language model) over proteomes only if genomes are added
backbone.hardware: CPU for the tabular meta-model; proteome embedding would be days on CPU

integration.partner_dataset: BacDive / NCBI type-strain genome assemblies, and BacDive's published genome-based trait predictions
integration.join_key: NCBI taxonomy ID (re-exported from bugphyzz; dropped in these CSVs)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: For which species and traits does what language models read about a microbe beat what its genome encodes, and does the crossover track how little has been written about it?

controls.positive_control: Accuracy must rise with Google hit count and self-rated knowledge; spore formation should be easier than biofilm formation.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle labels within trait; drop all LLM-confidence features and check gain disappears.
controls.external_validation: Train trust model on WA, test on the 15,257-species LA panel; or compare with BacDive genome-based predictions.

honest_claim_h3: Among bacterial species with bugphyzz annotations (mostly cultured type strains, some possibly inferred by phylogeny), the model predicts which LLM-generated trait calls agree with that curation, not whether they are biologically true.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the answers of many AI chatbots about a bacterial species, plus how famous it is, to predict which trait answers are right.
plain_idea.train_on: For each species and trait, the predictions of 18-31 language models, their self-rated knowledge level and the species' web hit count; 3,876 species, ~2,000-3,870 labels per main trait (verified).
plain_idea.predict: Whether the combined call matches the curated trait (Gram stain, motility, spore formation, etc.) recorded in bugphyzz, which collects lab-measured traits from BacDive and the literature.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Database curators could decide which machine-filled trait annotations to accept without checking; even failure would show that a simple majority vote is enough.

more_or_better_data.why: 3,876 well-annotated species is fewer than BacDive's 15,938 genome-linked strains used for genome-based random forests.

confidence_score.why: Many-model disagreement plus self-rated knowledge could give calibrated per-call confidence; the paper already reports knowledge-tier accuracy but not a calibrated probability.

models_beatable.why: Best single LLM ~0.77 mean balanced accuracy on a zero-shot run is beatable by stacking; genome-based 2025 models are recent and likely not.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Stacking sees more than any single LLM, but labels may be partly phylogeny-inferred and no new data measures the same trait the same way on the same split.

label_elsewhere.sources: BacDive (known resource, genome-linked strain phenotypes), bugphyzz full export (known; >60,000 taxa, includes inferred entries), Madin et al. trait compilation (known resource).
label_elsewhere.why: Curated traits exist for tens of thousands of other taxa, so any trust model can be checked on species outside this benchmark.

ambitious.why: Publishes microbial phenotype prediction methods; would need LLM-plus-genome combination clearly beating both on obscure species.

realistic.why: A calibrated filter for accepting LLM trait annotations, with a per-trait precision table.

fallback.why: A negative result (majority vote is as good as any learned filter) is still a short note.

pitch.headline: 727,000 scored LLM answers about 19,000 bacterial species, each with a curated truth label and the model's own confidence, in one MIT-licensed zip.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: 18-31 language models answering the same 10 traits for the same 3,876 species, plus self-rated knowledge and Google hit counts (verified in files); few benchmarks give this many models per item.
pitch.the_win: A learned filter that keeps ≥90% precision while retaining more calls than the paper's 'Extensive'-knowledge filter, beating the best single model's ~0.77 mean balanced accuracy.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: We learn that a simple majority vote or knowledge filter is all curators need, and how many labels are phylogeny-inferred rather than measured.
pitch.who_wants_it: BacDive (DSMZ) and bugphyzz (Waldron lab) curators deciding whether to import LLM-filled traits; the GenomeNet/HZI authors maintaining LLM-BioEval.

ml_idea: Stack the per-species predictions of many LLMs with self-rated knowledge and web hit counts into a calibrated accept/reject model per trait, evaluated on genus-held-out splits and transferred from the WA to the LA panel; optional extension joins BacDive genome-based predictions via NCBI taxonomy ID.

effort.compute_note: Estimated from file sizes (largest CSV 51 MB) and gradient-boosted trees on ~400k rows; nothing timed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Re-export the WA labels from bugphyzz with the Evidence column and count what fraction are 'asr'/inferred; if large, labels are partly a model's output.

verdict_reason: Data is clean, open and real, but the only ready task (deciding when to trust LLM trait calls) is a small step past the paper's own finding, no backbone fits name-only inputs, genome-based trait prediction is already well covered, and an unchecked share of the labels may be inferred from phylogeny.
